LoD studies were conducted by spiking in nucleic acid controls (Zeptometrix or ATCC) for all targets in all LRT specimen matrices at the concentrations reported in the package insert. Results A total of 51 lower respiratory tract (LRT) true-positive (TP) results and 17 LRT true-negative (TN) results were included in the cumulative performance analysis. For LRT specimens, false positives (FP) = 0 and false negatives (FN) = 0 following discrepancy resolution (specificity 100%, sensitivity 100%, total agreement 100%). Target-specific LRT performance demonstrated TP counts (n) for influenza A (5), including influenza A H1 (2) and influenza A H3 (3), influenza B (2), RSV A/B (4), human metapneumovirus (4), rhinovirus/enterovirus (4), adenovirus (7), parainfluenza virus 1 (6), parainfluenza virus 2 (2), parainfluenza virus 3 (5), parainfluenza virus 4 (5), SARS-CoV-2 (2), and Mycoplasma pneumoniae (5). LRT TN counts included influenza A (12), adenovirus (2), parainfluenza virus 3 (4), and Mycoplasma pneumoniae (5); other targets did not have LRT TN specimens available in the evaluated study set. LRT limit-of-detection verification met acceptance criteria (2/2 detected) for all evaluated targets at the designated concentrations, and sputolysin pre-treatment enabled reliable processing of viscous LRT samples without compromising expected detection. Conclusion The LIAISON PLEX Respiratory Flex Assay demonstrated acceptable clinical performance in lower respiratory specimens (BAL, bronchial wash, and endotracheal aspirate) when paired with standardized pre-analytic processing (sonication plus centrifugation) and sputolysin pre-treatment for mucoid samples. These data support the use of the assay for lower respiratory testing for respiratory pathogen detection in high-acuity clinical settings.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 LIAISON PLEX 呼吸道 Flex Assay(Diasorin)是一项 FDA 批准的、全自动样本到结果的 RT‐PCR 多重面板,已获批准用于鼻咽拭子(NPS)。由于下呼吸道(LRT)样本经常用于住院和免疫抑制患者的病毒性肺炎评估,我们验证了该 Assay 在 LRT 矩阵中的性能,重点关注支气管肺泡灌洗液(BAL)、支气管冲洗液(下呼吸道)和气管内吸引液(下呼吸道),以支持在批准样本类型之外的临床实施。方法 通过使用先前表征和人为构造的呼吸道样本(包括上呼吸道和 LRT 来源)评估准确性。LRT 样本包括 BAL(下呼吸道)和气管内吸引液(下呼吸道);鼻腔冲洗液也被评估为额外的液体矩阵。对于液体来源,比较了两种预分析流程:(1)超声处理后以 2700 rpm 离心 5 分钟;(2)超声处理后以 2000g 离心 10 分钟,使用上清液进行检测。Sputolysin pre‐治疗 在黏液性 LRT 液体中得到验证,以确保可吸管性。差异结果通过在 LIAISON PLEX 平台上重复检测和/或在常规实践中使用的比较平台(如 Verigene、ePlex、NxTAG RPP)进行确认检测来解决。分析灵敏度在 LRT 矩阵中通过在所有 LRT 样本矩阵中以包装说明书中报告的浓度加入核酸对照(Zeptometrix 或 ATCC)进行检测限(LoD)验证,针对代表性靶点(包括甲型流感病毒 H1、甲型流感病毒 H3、乙型流感病毒、呼吸道合胞病毒 A/B、人类副流感病毒、鼻病毒/肠道病毒、腺病毒和肺炎支原体)进行重复检测,接受标准为 2/2 检测到。结果 共计 51 个下呼吸道真阳性(TP)结果和 17 个下呼吸道真阴性(TN)结果被纳入累计性能分析。对于 LRT 样本,假阳性(FP)= 0,假阴性(FN)= 0,差异解决后,特异性 100%,敏感性 100%,总体一致性 100%。针对特定靶点的 LRT 性能显示 TP 计数(n):甲型流感病毒(5),包括甲型流感病毒 H1(2)和甲型流感病毒 H3(3),乙型流感病毒(2),呼吸道合胞病毒 A/B(4),人类副流感病毒(4),鼻病毒/肠道病毒(4),腺病毒(7),副流感病毒 1(6)、副流感病毒 2(2)、副流感病毒 3(5)、副流感病毒 4(5)、SARS‐CoV‐2(2)和肺炎支原体(5)。LRT TN 计数包括甲型流感病毒(12)、腺病毒(2)、副流感病毒 3(4)和肺炎支原体(5);其他靶点在评估研究集中未提供 LRT TN 样本。LRT 检测限验证满足所有评估靶点在指定浓度下的接受标准(2/2 检测到),Sputolysin pre‐治疗 使黏稠 LRT 样本可靠处理而不影响预期检测。结论 LIAISON PLEX 呼吸道 Flex Assay 在下呼吸道样本(BAL、支气管冲洗液和气管内吸引液)中表现出可接受的临床性能,当与标准化预分析处理(超声处理加离心)和 Sputolysin pre‐治疗 结合使用时,可用于高危临床环境中的呼吸道病原体检测。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在验证 LIAISON PLEX 呼吸道 Flex Assay 在下呼吸道(LRT)样本中的适用性,LRT 样本常用于住院和免疫抑制患者的病毒性肺炎诊断。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究评估了 LIAISON PLEX 呼吸道 Flex Assay 在 LRT 样本(包括支气管肺泡灌洗液(BAL)、支气管冲洗液和气管内吸引液)以及鼻腔冲洗液(作为额外液体矩阵)中的性能。
analysis_zh.methods: 准确性通过使用先前表征和人为构造的呼吸道样本(包括上呼吸道和 LRT 来源)进行评估。对于液体来源,比较了两种预分析流程:(1)超声处理后以 2700 rpm 离心 5 分钟;(2)超声处理后以 2000g 离心 10 分钟,使用上清液进行检测。差异结果通过在 LIAISON PLEX 平台上重复检测和/或在常规实践中使用的比较平台(如 Verigene、ePlex、NxTAG RPP)进行确认检测来解决。

analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果为 LIAISON PLEX 呼吸道 Flex Assay 在诊断 呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)和其他呼吸道病原体的下呼吸道样本中的临床实施提供信息,对管理高危患者群体中的病毒性肺炎至关重要。

papers.title: Association of RSV Vaccination With Clinical Outcomes in Older Adults With Heart Failure: A Propensity‐Matched Analysis
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is increasingly recognized as a trigger for adverse outcomes in older adults with heart failure (HF). Following FDA approval of RSV vaccines for adults ≥ 60 years in 2023, real‐world evidence in HF populations remains limited. Methods We conducted a multicenter retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX US Collaborative Network. Adults ≥ 60 years with HF were identified and stratified by RSV vaccination status from May 1, 2023, to January 01, 2026. Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed. The primary outcome was all‐cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included respiratory failure, healthcare utilization, and cardiovascular events. Results After PSM, 777 vaccinated and 777 unvaccinated HF patients were analyzed. All‐cause mortality (HR 0.51, 95% CI, 0.33−0.79) and ICU admissions were significantly lower in vaccinated patients (2.7% vs. 5.8%, HR 0.46, 95% CI 0.25–0.86), while healthcare utilization was significantly higher in the vaccinated cohort (HR 1.85, 95% CI 1.65–2.08). No significant differences were observed in respiratory failure (7.3% vs. 9.4%, HR 0.87, 95% CI 0.61–1.23), inpatient or emergency visits (29.9% vs. 35.1%, HR 0.97, 95% CI 0.81–1.16), HF exacerbations, myocardial infarction, or stroke. Age‐stratified subgroup analyses (60–75 and 75–90 years) showed consistent findings, with no significant cardiovascular differences and significantly higher healthcare utilization in vaccinated patients across both age groups. Conclusions In older adults with HF, RSV vaccination was associated with lower mortality and fewer ICU admissions, without a corresponding reduction in overall inpatient/emergency use or acute‐care utilization. These findings are hypothesis‐generating and may reflect prevention of severe respiratory illness.

Following FDA approval of RSV vaccines for adults ≥ 60 years in 2023, real‐world evidence in HF populations remains limited.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A multicenter retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX US Collaborative Network was conducted. Adults ≥ 60 years with HF were identified and stratified by RSV vaccination status from May 1, 2023, to January 01, 2026.
analysis.methods: Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed. The primary outcome was all‐cause mortality, and secondary outcomes included respiratory failure, healthcare utilization, and cardiovascular events.

analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that RSV vaccination was associated with lower mortality and fewer ICU admissions in older adults with HF, without a corresponding reduction in overall inpatient/emergency use or acute‐care utilization.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings may inform future studies on the prevention of severe respiratory illness in older adults with HF and suggest potential benefits of RSV vaccination in this population.

Results showed significantly lower mortality and ICU admissions in vaccinated patients, but higher healthcare utilization. The authors suggest these findings may reflect prevention of severe respiratory illness. The study's limitations include its observational design and potential confounding factors, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that RSV vaccination was associated with lower mortality and fewer ICU admissions in older adults with HF, without a corresponding reduction in overall inpatient/emergency use or acute‐care utilization.

papers.title_zh: 呼吸道合胞病毒与心力衰竭老年患者临床结局的关联:一项倾向匹配分析
papers.source_body_en: ABSTRACT Background Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is increasingly recognized as a trigger for adverse outcomes in older adults with heart failure (HF). Following FDA approval of RSV vaccines for adults ≥ 60 years in 2023, real‐world evidence in HF populations remains limited. Methods We conducted a multicenter retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX US Collaborative Network. Adults ≥ 60 years with HF were identified and stratified by RSV vaccination status from May 1, 2023, to January 01, 2026. Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed. The primary outcome was all‐cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included respiratory failure, healthcare utilization, and cardiovascular events. Results After PSM, 777 vaccinated and 777 unvaccinated HF patients were analyzed. All‐cause mortality (HR 0.51, 95% CI, 0.33−0.79) and ICU admissions were significantly lower in vaccinated patients (2.7% vs. 5.8%, HR 0.46, 95% CI 0.25–0.86), while healthcare utilization was significantly higher in the vaccinated cohort (HR 1.85, 95% CI 1.65–2.08). No significant differences were observed in respiratory failure (7.3% vs. 9.4%, HR 0.87, 95% CI 0.61–1.23), inpatient or emergency visits (29.9% vs. 35.1%, HR 0.97, 95% CI 0.81–1.16), HF exacerbations, myocardial infarction, or stroke. Age‐stratified subgroup analyses (60–75 and 75–90 years) showed consistent findings, with no significant cardiovascular differences and significantly higher healthcare utilization in vaccinated patients across both age groups. Conclusions In older adults with HF, RSV vaccination was associated with lower mortality and fewer ICU admissions, without a corresponding reduction in overall inpatient/emergency use or acute‐care utilization. These findings are hypothesis‐generating and may reflect prevention of severe respiratory illness.

papers.title: Postpandemic Trends in Pediatric Respiratory Virus Hospitalizations: A Multicenter Study, 2019-2025.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: The COVID-19 pandemic profoundly altered the circulation of respiratory viruses in children, changing the epidemiology of acute lower respiratory tract infections. In the postpandemic period, respiratory pathogens showed marked temporal variability. The 2024-2025 season was the first respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) season in Italy during which RSV immunoprophylaxis with nirsevimab was implemented, allowing evaluation of recent trends in pediatric hospitalizations. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective multicenter study across 16 pediatric hospitals in Italy. Hospitalizations of children younger than 18 years with RSV, influenza, adenovirus, parainfluenza virus, rhinovirus infection, or bronchiolitis of unspecified viral etiology were identified from January 2019 to March 2025 using ICD-9-CM diagnostic codes. Annual and monthly hospitalization rates per 100,000 children were calculated using national demographic data. Temporal trends were assessed across six consecutive seasons. RESULTS: Overall, 23,981 hospitalizations were recorded. RSV was the most frequent pathogen (42.5%), followed by influenza (18.6%), adenovirus (9.9%), and rhinovirus (7.3%). Hospitalizations declined sharply in 2020 and subsequently increased, peaking in 2024 (n = 4903; +30.8% vs. During the 2024-2025 season, total admissions decreased by 17.2% compared with 2023-2024 (3390 vs. 4095), mainly due to a marked reduction in RSV-related hospitalizations (-41.6%, 1230 vs. 2107), with modest increases in influenza-, adenovirus-, and rhinovirus-associated admissions. CONCLUSIONS: This nationwide analysis describes postpandemic trends in pediatric respiratory virus hospitalizations in Italy, highlighting changing pathogen-specific patterns and the need for continued viral surveillance.

papers.title: Trends in all-cause pneumonia and influenza hospitalization incidence by coding position - a study of US healthcare claims, 2014-2023.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: The hospitalization rate for pneumonia among adults has decreased in the U.S. since the early 2000's. The increasing prevalence of chronic conditions among adults, especially those associated with risk factors for pneumonia caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae, influenza and respiratory syncytial virus, may be contributing to a larger population susceptible to pneumonia. Existing estimates utilizing claims data may underestimate the true rates of disease due to how diagnostic coding fields are used to define outcomes. METHODS: A retrospective descriptive study of adult (> 18 years) ACPI inpatient hospitalizations was conducted using US healthcare claims data from 2014 to 2023. Principal ACPI hospitalizations were defined as those with a principal field code for ACPI only. Expanded principal ACPI hospitalizations were those with a principal code for ACPI or a principal code for sepsis, meningitis, COPD, empyema, and acute respiratory failure in combination with a secondary code for ACPI. Prevalence of risk factors indicative for pneumococcal pneumonia, RSV, or severe influenza vaccination were assessed. RESULTS: Principal ACPI showed the largest decline in incidence and this decline was greatest among the younger age groups compared to the older adults. In contrast, the expanded principal definition of ACPI captured between 48.5 and 63.4% of ACPI codes present in any field and showed lower variation over time compared to the principal definition. The proportion of adults with a risk factor of interest increased during the study period, particularly between 2020 and 2023. Greater than 96% of adults ≥ 65y hospitalized with ACPI in 2023 had at least one risk factor indicative for vaccination against pneumococcal, influenza, or RSV in the 3 years prior. CONCLUSIONS: We show that using only principal diagnostic codes to identify ACPI hospitalization may disproportionately inflate the decline in ACPI hospitalizations between 2014 and 2023. Using a principal ACPI hospitalization definition would exclude approximately 30% of hospitalizations that would meet the expanded principal ACPI definition. The shift towards greater use of sepsis and COPD codes in the principal diagnostic code position may be attributed to coding changes over the study period. Risk factors for pneumonia increased in prevalence, particularly during the COVID-19 pandemic period.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate trends in pneumonia and influenza hospitalization incidence by coding position, particularly focusing on the potential underestimation of disease rates due to diagnostic coding practices. The background highlights the decreasing hospitalization rate for pneumonia among adults in the U.S. since the early 2000's and the increasing prevalence of chronic conditions that may contribute to a larger susceptible population.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective descriptive study of adult (> 18 years) ACPI inpatient hospitalizations was conducted using US healthcare claims data from 2014 to 2023. The study focused on hospitalizations with a principal field code for ACPI or related conditions such as sepsis, meningitis, COPD, empyema, and acute respiratory failure.
analysis.methods: The study used healthcare claims data to define principal and expanded principal ACPI hospitalizations. Risk factors for pneumococcal pneumonia, RSV, or severe influenza were assessed based on the presence of specific codes in the data.
analysis.main_results: Principal ACPI hospitalizations showed the largest decline in incidence, with the greatest reduction among younger age groups. The expanded principal definition captured between 48.5 and 63.4% of all ACPI codes present in any field and showed less variation over time compared to the principal definition. The proportion of adults with risk factors increased during the study period, especially between 2020 and 2023.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that using only principal diagnostic codes may disproportionately inflate the decline in ACPI hospitalizations between 2014 and 2023. They noted that the shift in coding practices may be due to changes in how sepsis and COPD are coded during the study period.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that current methods of estimating disease rates using principal diagnostic codes may not accurately reflect the true incidence of pneumonia and influenza. This has implications for surveillance and the understanding of disease trends in public health.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on diagnostic coding practices, which may not fully capture the true disease rates. The evidence is moderate, as it is based on claims data and does not account for potential biases in coding.

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed trends in all-cause pneumonia and influenza hospitalization incidence in the U.S. from 2014 to 2023, focusing on the impact of diagnostic coding practices. It found that principal ACPI hospitalizations showed the largest decline, particularly among younger adults, while the expanded principal definition captured a broader range of cases with less variation over time. The authors suggest that the shift in coding practices may have influenced these trends, highlighting the need for more accurate methods in disease surveillance. The study's findings have implications for public health, as they indicate potential underestimation of disease rates using current coding systems. However, the study is limited by its reliance on claims data and the possibility of coding biases.

papers.title_zh: 所有原因肺炎和流感住院趋势发病率按编码位置分析——基于美国医疗索赔数据的研究,2014-2023年。
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: The hospitalization rate for pneumonia among adults has decreased in the U.S. since the early 2000's. The increasing prevalence of chronic conditions among adults, especially those associated with risk factors for pneumonia caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae, influenza and respiratory syncytial virus, may be contributing to a larger population susceptible to pneumonia. Existing estimates utilizing claims data may underestimate the true rates of disease due to how diagnostic coding fields are used to define outcomes. METHODS: A retrospective descriptive study of adult (> 18 years) ACPI inpatient hospitalizations was conducted using US healthcare claims data from 2014 to 2023. Principal ACPI hospitalizations were defined as those with a principal field code for ACPI only. Expanded principal ACPI hospitalizations were those with a principal code for ACPI or a principal code for sepsis, meningitis, COPD, empyema, and acute respiratory failure in combination with a secondary code for ACPI. Prevalence of risk factors indicative for pneumococcal pneumonia, RSV, or severe influenza vaccination were assessed. RESULTS: Principal ACPI showed the largest decline in incidence and this decline was greatest among the younger age groups compared to the older adults. In contrast, the expanded principal definition of ACPI captured between 48.5 and 63.4% of ACPI codes present in any field and showed lower variation over time compared to the principal definition. The proportion of adults with a risk factor of interest increased during the study period, particularly between 2020 and 2023. Greater than 96% of adults ≥ 65y hospitalized with ACPI in 2023 had at least one risk factor indicative for vaccination against pneumococcal, influenza, or RSV in the 3 years prior. CONCLUSIONS: We show that using only principal diagnostic codes to identify ACPI hospitalization may disproportionately inflate the decline in ACPI hospitalizations between 2014 and 2023. Using a principal ACPI hospitalization definition would exclude approximately 30% of hospitalizations that would meet the expanded principal ACPI definition. The shift towards greater use of sepsis and COPD codes in the principal diagnostic code position may be attributed to coding changes over the study period. Risk factors for pneumonia increased in prevalence, particularly during the COVID-19 pandemic period.

papers.title: Mortality and vaccine-preventable deaths from severe acute respiratory infections in Brazil in 2026
papers.abstract: Background: A large increase in mortality from severe acute respiratory infections (SARI) in Brazil in 2025 was mainly driven by influenza A and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) among children and the aged, but 2026 data remain largely unpublished. Methods: Secondary data on SARI by age group (<2, 2-4, 5-14, 15-49, 50-64, 65+ years) and virus (Influenza A/B, RSV, SARS-CoV-2, adenovirus, rhinovirus, bocavirus, and metapneumovirus) were retrieved for 35 weeks of 2026. Weekly variations in infection rate (IR) and mortality rate (MR) were described by virus and age group. Case fatality ratio (CFR) and vaccine-preventable deaths from influenza, RSV, and SARS-CoV-2 were analysed by age group. Missing virus classification was estimated by multinomial regression. Poisson-based 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated for MR. Results: Influenza A infections quintupled during February and March, with a mortality peak in April, mainly due to H2N3. RSV and rhinovirus caused more deaths than influenza viruses, especially among young children (<2) and the aged (65+). The former were most frequently infected by RSV and the latter by rhinovirus. For those 50 years or older, influenza B reached a CFR of about 20%, compared with 5-15% for influenza A, metapneumovirus, rhinovirus, and other non-subtyped viruses. The highest vaccine-preventable MRs per 100,000 were 17.23 for the oldest and 8.62 for the youngest. Under ideal conditions, 6418 lives could have been saved, about half among children and adolescents <15 years old. Conclusions: Vaccine-preventable SARI in Brazil exerted a high toll in fall and winter 2026, mainly due to influenza A, RSV, and rhinovirus. Better vaccine coverage may significantly reduce this toll.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to assess the impact of vaccine-preventable severe acute respiratory infections (SARI) in Brazil in 2026, particularly focusing on the mortality burden from respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and other pathogens.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used secondary data on SARI cases by age group and virus type, collected over 35 weeks in 2026, to analyze mortality rates and vaccine-preventable deaths.
analysis.methods: The researchers described weekly variations in infection and mortality rates by virus and age group, calculated Poisson-based 95% confidence intervals for mortality rates, and estimated missing virus classifications using multinomial regression.
analysis.main_results: Influenza A infections increased fivefold during February and March, with a mortality peak in April mainly due to H2N3. RSV and rhinovirus caused more deaths than influenza viruses, especially among young children (<2) and the aged (65+). The highest vaccine-preventable mortality rates per 100,000 were 17.23 for the oldest and 8.62 for the youngest.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight the significant mortality burden from RSV and other SARI pathogens, particularly in vulnerable age groups, and emphasize the potential impact of improved vaccine coverage.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results inform the need for targeted vaccination strategies and improved surveillance for RSV and other vaccine-preventable SARI pathogens in Brazil, especially among children and the elderly.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on secondary data and does not provide detailed laboratory or statistical procedures, which may limit the depth of analysis. However, the evidence is strong given the comprehensive data on mortality and infection rates.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the mortality and vaccine-preventable deaths from severe acute respiratory infections (SARI) in Brazil during 2026, with a focus on respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). It reports that RSV and rhinovirus caused more deaths than influenza viruses, particularly among young children and the elderly. The highest vaccine-preventable mortality rates were observed in the oldest age group. The study suggests that better vaccine coverage could significantly reduce this toll. While the analysis is based on secondary data and lacks detailed statistical procedures, the findings are robust and highlight the importance of addressing RSV and other SARI pathogens in public health strategies.

papers.title: From Selective Prophylaxis to Broad Infant RSV Protection: A Bibliometric Analysis and Evidence Gap Map, 1998-2025.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Infant respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) prevention has moved from selective palivizumab prophylaxis toward broader protection through long-acting monoclonal antibodies and maternal vaccination. We examined how this research area evolved and whether original studies address evidence needed for implementation at scale. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a bibliometric analysis and evidence-gap mapping study of Web of Science Core Collection records from 1998 to 2025. The bibliometric corpus included 2004 publications; 1581 original articles underwent relevance screening and targeted audit, yielding 1227 studies for evidence-gap mapping. Analyses compared 1998-2022 with 2023-2025. A random sample of 150 articles was used to validate relevance screening. RESULTS: Publication output rose sharply after 2022, with 2023-2025 accounting for 35.0% of the bibliometric corpus. Earlier work centered on palivizumab, preterm infants, and hospitalization; recent studies increasingly addressed nirsevimab, maternal RSV vaccination, implementation, and vaccine candidates. Hospitalization outcomes, disease burden, monoclonal antibody strategies, and real-world effectiveness were well represented, whereas coverage/uptake, acceptance, equity, safety monitoring, economic evaluation, applicability to low- and middle-income countries, and coordination between maternal vaccination and infant monoclonal antibodies were less common. Validation showed 86.7% agreement (Cohen's kappa = 0.52). CONCLUSIONS: The literature has shifted toward broad infant RSV protection, but implementation-relevant evidence remains uneven. Comparative and program-level research is needed to determine how maternal vaccination and infant monoclonal antibody strategies can be implemented and coordinated across health systems while minimizing missed opportunities for protection.

papers.title_zh: 从选择性预防到广泛婴儿呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)保护:1998-2025年的文献计量分析与证据缺口图
papers.source_body_en: OBJECTIVES: Infant respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) prevention has moved from selective palivizumab prophylaxis toward broader protection through long-acting monoclonal antibodies and maternal vaccination. We examined how this research area evolved and whether original studies address evidence needed for implementation at scale. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a bibliometric analysis and evidence-gap mapping study of Web of Science Core Collection records from 1998 to 2025. The bibliometric corpus included 2004 publications; 1581 original articles underwent relevance screening and targeted audit, yielding 1227 studies for evidence-gap mapping. Analyses compared 1998-2022 with 2023-2025. A random sample of 150 articles was used to validate relevance screening. RESULTS: Publication output rose sharply after 2022, with 2023-2025 accounting for 35.0% of the bibliometric corpus. Earlier work centered on palivizumab, preterm infants, and hospitalization; recent studies increasingly addressed nirsevimab, maternal RSV vaccination, implementation, and vaccine candidates. Hospitalization outcomes, disease burden, monoclonal antibody strategies, and real-world effectiveness were well represented, whereas coverage/uptake, acceptance, equity, safety monitoring, economic evaluation, applicability to low- and middle-income countries, and coordination between maternal vaccination and infant monoclonal antibodies were less common. Validation showed 86.7% agreement (Cohen's kappa = 0.52). CONCLUSIONS: The literature has shifted toward broad infant RSV protection, but implementation-relevant evidence remains uneven. Comparative and program-level research is needed to determine how maternal vaccination and infant monoclonal antibody strategies can be implemented and coordinated across health systems while minimizing missed opportunities for protection.
papers.abstract_zh: OBJECTIVES: 婴儿呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)预防研究已从选择性使用帕利珠单抗(palivizumab)预防转向通过长效单克隆抗体和母体呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)免疫策略实现更广泛的保护。我们考察了这一研究领域的发展历程,并评估原始研究是否满足大规模实施所需的证据。MATERIALS AND METHODS: 我们对1998年至2025年Web of Science核心合集中的文献进行了文献计量分析和证据缺口图研究,文献计量语料库包含2004篇文献;1581篇原始文章经过相关性筛选和针对性审核,最终获得1227项研究用于证据缺口图分析。分析比较了1998-2022年与2023-2025年的数据。通过随机选取150篇文章验证了相关性筛选过程。RESULTS: 2022年后文献产出显著增加,2023-2025年占文献计量语料库的35.0%。早期研究主要集中在帕利珠单抗、早产儿和住院治疗方面;近期研究则越来越多地涉及母体呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)免疫策略、实施策略以及婴儿单克隆抗体候选药物。住院治疗结果、疾病负担、单克隆抗体策略和真实世界有效性在文献中得到了充分反映,而覆盖率/接受度、公平性、安全性监测、经济评估、在低收入和中等收入国家的应用以及母体呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)免疫策略与婴儿单克隆抗体策略之间的协调性则较少涉及。验证结果显示86.7%的一致性(Cohen's kappa = 0.52)。CONCLUSIONS: 文献已转向广泛婴儿RSV保护,但与实施相关的证据仍不均衡。需要进行比较研究和项目层面的研究,以确定如何在不同卫生系统中实施和协调母体呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)免疫策略与婴儿单克隆抗体策略,同时最大限度地减少保护机会的遗漏。

papers.title: RSV & rhinovirus coinfection order dictates outcome via type III interferon-mediated interference in infant respiratory epithelium
papers.abstract: Coinfection with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and rhinovirus (RV) is the most frequently detected coinfection in infants, yet mechanisms governing viral interference and disease outcome remain poorly understood. Although infection order is a key determinant of coinfection outcome involving RSV, influenza, rhinovirus, and SARS-CoV-2, its role in RSV/RV coinfections has not been defined. Using infant-derived human nasal organoids at air-liquid interface, we demonstrate that coinfection order fundamentally determines the outcome of RSV/RV interactions. An initial RSV infection almost completely inhibits secondary RV coinfection, whereas primary RV infection only partially impairs a subsequent RSV coinfection. These distinct outcomes are accompanied by divergent temporal antiviral and pro-inflammatory responses. Mechanistically, we identify type III interferons as a sufficient mediator of RSV-induced restriction of RV, establishing a host-driven mechanism of viral interference. In contrast, partial impairment of RSV following RV infection occurs through an interferon-independent mechanism. Despite marked differences, RSV/RV coinfections do not exacerbate epithelial injury or innate immune responses beyond that induced by RSV alone, indicating RSV is the dominant driver of pathology in coinfections. Collectively, our data establishes coinfection order as a critical determinant of RSV/RV outcome and reveals novel and mechanistic insight into critical viral-host interactions in the infant nasal epithelium.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand the mechanisms governing viral interference and disease outcome in RSV and rhinovirus (RV) coinfections in infants, given that coinfection with these viruses is common but the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used infant-derived human nasal organoids at air-liquid interface to investigate the impact of infection order on RSV and RV coinfections.
analysis.methods: Infant-derived human nasal organoids were used to demonstrate the impact of coinfection order on RSV and RV interactions, focusing on antiviral and pro-inflammatory responses.
analysis.main_results: An initial RSV infection almost completely inhibits secondary RV coinfection, whereas primary RV infection only partially impairs a subsequent RSV coinfection. These outcomes are accompanied by divergent temporal antiviral and pro-inflammatory responses.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study identifies type III interferons as a key mediator of RSV-induced restriction of RV, establishing a host-driven mechanism of viral interference. Partial impairment of RSV following RV infection occurs through an interferon-independent mechanism.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide novel mechanistic insight into critical viral-host interactions in the infant nasal epithelium, which could inform surveillance, diagnosis, and treatment strategies for RSV and RV coinfections.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by the use of organoids, which may not fully replicate in vivo conditions. The findings suggest that RSV is the dominant driver of pathology in coinfections, but further research is needed to confirm these results in vivo.

analysis.summary_en: This study used infant-derived human nasal organoids to investigate the impact of infection order on RSV and RV coinfections, revealing that RSV almost completely inhibits secondary RV coinfection while RV only partially impairs RSV. Type III interferons were identified as a key mediator of RSV-induced restriction of RV, providing novel mechanistic insight into viral-host interactions in the infant nasal epithelium.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在了解RSV和鼻病毒(RV)共同感染在婴儿中调控病毒干扰和疾病结局的机制,鉴于这些病毒的共同感染很常见,但其潜在机制仍不清楚。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究使用来源于婴儿的人类鼻腔类器官在气液界面条件下,探讨感染顺序对RSV和RV共同感染的影响。
elements_zh.methods: 使用来源于婴儿的人类鼻腔类器官,以展示感染顺序对RSV和RV相互作用的影响,重点关注III型干扰素和促炎反应。
elements_zh.main_results: 初始的RSV感染几乎完全抑制了随后的RV共同感染,而初始的RV感染仅部分抑制随后的RSV共同感染。这些结果伴随着不同的时间序列上的III型干扰素和促炎反应。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 本研究鉴定出III型干扰素作为RSV诱导限制RV的介质,建立了一种由RSV驱动的病毒干扰机制。RV感染后RSV的部分抑制是通过干扰素独立机制实现的。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为婴儿鼻腔上皮中关键的病毒-III型干扰素相互作用提供了新的机制性见解,这可能有助于制定针对RSV和RV共同感染的抗病毒药物、治疗策略和疫苗接种策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于使用了类器官,可能无法完全模拟体内条件。研究结果表明RSV是共同感染中病理的主导驱动因素,但需要进一步的研究在体内确认这些结果。

papers.abstract_zh: RSV与鼻病毒(RV)的共同感染是婴儿中最常检测到的共同感染,然而调控病毒干扰和疾病结局的机制仍不清楚。尽管感染顺序是决定RSV、流感病毒、鼻病毒和SARS-CoV-2共同感染结局的关键因素,但其在RSV/RV共同感染中的作用尚未明确。我们使用来源于婴儿的人类鼻腔类器官,在气液界面条件下,证明共同感染顺序从根本上决定了RSV/RV相互作用的结局。初始的RSV感染几乎完全抑制了随后的RV共同感染,而初始的RV感染仅部分抑制随后的RSV共同感染。这些不同的结局伴随着不同的时间序列上的III型干扰素和促炎反应。机制上,我们鉴定出III型干扰素作为RSV诱导限制RV的充分介质,建立了一种由RSV驱动的病毒干扰机制。相反,RV感染后RSV的部分抑制是通过干扰素独立机制实现的。尽管存在显著差异,RSV/RV共同感染并未加剧上皮损伤或先天免疫应答,超过RSV单独引起的程度,表明RSV是共同感染中病理的主导驱动因素。综上所述,我们的数据确立了共同感染顺序作为RSV/RV结局的关键决定因素,并揭示了婴儿鼻腔上皮中关键病毒-III型干扰素相互作用的新机制和机理见解。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在了解RSV和鼻病毒(RV)共同感染在婴儿中调控病毒干扰和疾病结局的机制,鉴于这些病毒的共同感染很常见,但其潜在机制仍不清楚。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究使用来源于婴儿的人类鼻腔类器官在气液界面条件下,探讨感染顺序对RSV和RV共同感染的影响。
analysis_zh.methods: 使用来源于婴儿的人类鼻腔类器官,以展示感染顺序对RSV和RV相互作用的影响,重点关注III型干扰素和促炎反应。
analysis_zh.main_results: 初始的RSV感染几乎完全抑制了随后的RV共同感染,而初始的RV感染仅部分抑制随后的RSV共同感染。这些结果伴随着不同的时间序列上的III型干扰素和促炎反应。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 本研究鉴定出III型干扰素作为RSV诱导限制RV的介质,建立了一种由RSV驱动的病毒干扰机制。RV感染后RSV的部分抑制是通过干扰素独立机制实现的。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为婴儿鼻腔上皮中关键的病毒-III型干扰素相互作用提供了新的机制性见解,这可能有助于制定针对RSV和RV共同感染的抗病毒药物、治疗策略和疫苗接种策略。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于使用了类器官,可能无法完全模拟体内条件。研究结果表明RSV是共同感染中病理的主导驱动因素,但需要进一步的研究在体内确认这些结果。

papers.title: Plasmonic biosensor platforms for next-generation personalized medical diagnostics
papers.abstract: The increasing healthcare burden demands precise diagnostics for early detection and longitudinal disease monitoring. Although conventional assays such as ELISA and PCR offer precision, they require intensive sample preparation, bulkier instrumentation and prolonged assay times. This review examines plasmonic biosensors as a transformative alternative for personalized and point-of-care diagnostics. We comprehensively examine recent advancements, such as the integration of nanomaterials, microfabrication strategies, advanced surface chemistry and prototype miniaturization, and consider examples for the detection of cancer biomarkers (microRNA-21 and alpha-fetoprotein), viral proteins (respiratory syncytial virus and SARS-CoV-2), and inflammatory biomarkers (C-reactive protein). Furthermore, we address the critical aspects that hinder the clinical translation of plasmonic biosensors. The review concludes that, despite significant laboratory-scale progress, standardized manufacturing, scalable nanofabrication and the inclusion of artificial intelligence/machine learning frameworks remain essential for the widespread utilization of plasmonic technology in personalized medicine and diagnostics.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on plasmonic biosensors as a transformative alternative for personalized and point-of-care diagnostics, particularly for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and its associated infections.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review evaluates recent advancements in plasmonic biosensors, including nanomaterials, microfabrication strategies, advanced surface chemistry, and prototype miniaturization, with examples for detecting RSV and other pathogens.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that, despite significant laboratory-scale progress, standardized manufacturing, scalable nanofabrication, and the inclusion of artificial intelligence/machine learning frameworks are essential for the widespread utilization of plasmonic technology in personalized medicine and diagnostics.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights the need for standardized manufacturing and scalable nanofabrication, indicating that these areas remain unresolved and require further investigation.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that future research should focus on standardized manufacturing, scalable nanofabrication, and integrating AI/ML frameworks to enhance the clinical translation of plasmonic biosensors for RSV diagnostics.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores plasmonic biosensors as a promising alternative to conventional diagnostic methods for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). It highlights the advantages of plasmonic biosensors, such as their potential for personalized and point-of-care diagnostics, and discusses recent advancements in nanomaterials, microfabrication, and surface chemistry. The review emphasizes the importance of standardized manufacturing, scalable nanofabrication, and AI/ML integration for clinical application. Despite laboratory progress, challenges in these areas remain unresolved, underscoring the need for further research to enable widespread use of plasmonic technology in RSV diagnostics.

elements_en.scope_and_question: The review focuses on plasmonic biosensors as a transformative alternative for personalized and point-of-care diagnostics, particularly for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and its associated infections.
elements_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review evaluates recent advancements in plasmonic biosensors, including nanomaterials, microfabrication strategies, advanced surface chemistry, and prototype miniaturization, with examples for detecting RSV and other pathogens.
elements_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that, despite significant laboratory-scale progress, standardized manufacturing, scalable nanofabrication, and the inclusion of artificial intelligence/machine learning frameworks are essential for the widespread utilization of plasmonic technology in personalized medicine and diagnostics.
elements_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights the need for standardized manufacturing and scalable nanofabrication, indicating that these areas remain unresolved and require further investigation.
elements_en.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that future research should focus on standardized manufacturing, scalable nanofabrication, and integrating AI/ML frameworks to enhance the clinical translation of plasmonic biosensors for RSV diagnostics.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述聚焦于等离激元生物传感器作为个性化和即时检测诊断的变革性替代方案,特别是针对呼吸道合胞病毒(呼吸道合胞病毒RSV)及其相关感染。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本综述评估了等离激元生物传感器的近期进展,包括纳米材料、微加工策略、先进的表面化学以及原型微型化,并以检测RSV和其他病原体为例。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 综述得出结论,尽管在实验室规模上取得了显著进展,但标准化制造、可扩展的纳米加工以及引入人工智能/机器学习框架对于等离激元技术在个性化医学和诊断中的广泛应用仍然是必不可少的。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 综述强调了标准化制造和可扩展纳米加工的重要性,指出这些领域仍存在未解决的问题,需要进一步研究。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 综述建议未来的研究应聚焦于标准化制造、可扩展纳米加工以及将AI/ML框架整合到等离激元生物传感器中,以提高其在RSV诊断中的临床转化能力。}}.{

papers.title_zh: 下一代个性化医疗诊断的等离激元生物传感器平台
papers.source_body_en: The increasing healthcare burden demands precise diagnostics for early detection and longitudinal disease monitoring. Although conventional assays such as ELISA and PCR offer precision, they require intensive sample preparation, bulkier instrumentation and prolonged assay times. This review examines plasmonic biosensors as a transformative alternative for personalized and point-of-care diagnostics. We comprehensively examine recent advancements, such as the integration of nanomaterials, microfabrication strategies, advanced surface chemistry and prototype miniaturization, and consider examples for the detection of cancer biomarkers (microRNA-21 and alpha-fetoprotein), viral proteins (respiratory syncytial virus and SARS-CoV-2), and inflammatory biomarkers (C-reactive protein). Furthermore, we address the critical aspects that hinder the clinical translation of plasmonic biosensors. The review concludes that, despite significant laboratory-scale progress, standardized manufacturing, scalable nanofabrication and the inclusion of artificial intelligence/machine learning frameworks remain essential for the widespread utilization of plasmonic technology in personalized medicine and diagnostics.
papers.abstract_zh: 日益增长的医疗负担要求精确的诊断以实现早期检测和疾病长期监测。尽管传统的检测方法如ELISA和PCR具有较高的精确度,但它们需要繁琐的样本制备、较大的仪器设备以及较长的检测时间。本综述探讨了等离激元生物传感器作为个性化和即时检测(point-of-care)诊断的变革性替代方案。我们全面审视了近期的进展,例如纳米材料的整合、微加工策略、先进的表面化学以及原型微型化,并考虑了用于检测癌症生物标志物(microRNA-21和甲胎蛋白)、病毒蛋白(呼吸道合胞病毒和SARS-CoV-2)以及炎症生物标志物(C-反应蛋白)的例子。此外,我们还讨论了阻碍等离激元生物传感器临床转化的关键因素。综述得出结论,尽管在实验室规模上取得了显著进展,但标准化制造、可扩展的纳米加工以及引入人工智能/机器学习框架仍然是等离激元技术在个性化医学和诊断中广泛应用所必需的。

Search Home Health and social care Public health Health protection Immunisation Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) maternal vaccination coverage in England UK Health Security Agency Official Statistics Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) maternal vaccination coverage in England: May 2026 report Updated 1 October 2026 Applies to England Contents Main points Help us improve this resource Analysis of maternal RSV vaccine uptake Data sources and methodology Background information Further information and contact details Print this page © Crown copyright 2026 This publication is licensed under the terms of the Open Government Licence v3.0 except where otherwise stated. To view this licence, visit nationalarchives.gov.uk/doc/open-government-licence/version/3 or write to the Information Policy Team, The National Archives, Kew, London TW9 4DU, or email: psi@nationalarchives.gov.uk. Where we have identified any third party copyright information you will need to obtain permission from the copyright holders concerned. This publication is available at https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/respiratory-syncytial-virus-rsv-maternal-vaccination-coverage-in-england/respiratory-syncytial-virus-rsv-maternal-vaccination-coverage-in-england-may-2026-report Published 1 October 2026 This report presents monthly vaccine uptake data for the maternal respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) immunisation programme in England, focusing on the period up to May 2026. This report includes vaccine uptake estimates for pregnant women who delivered in the twenty-first month of the maternal vaccination programme in May 2026. Main points The main messages of this report are: 62.2% (26,174 out of 42,107) of women who reported giving birth during the survey month received an RSV vaccine uptake varied by NHS commissioning region, with the highest uptake reported in the South West region (72.3%) and the lowest in the London region (54.8%) uptake varied across integrated care boards (ICBs) with the highest uptake reported in the Norfolk and Waveney ICB (76.3%) and the lowest in Birmingham and Solihull ICB (41.1%) uptake varied across local authorities with the highest uptake reported in West Berkshire (82.3%) and the lowest in Walsall (35.9%) uptake varied by ethnic group, with the highest uptake reported among the Asian or Asian British - Chinese ethnic group (78.5%) and the lowest among the Black - Caribbean ethnic group (39.2%) Help us improve this resource This vaccine uptake report has been designated as an Official Statistics release. As part of this process, we are seeking feedback from users to ensure the publication meets your needs. We would be grateful if you could take a few minutes to complete a short survey and share your views. Please complete the survey Your input will play an important role in shaping the development of this publication. Thank you for your time and support. Analysis of maternal RSV vaccine uptake Maternal uptake of the RSV vaccine is assessed monthly to monitor the reach and impact of the national immunisation programme. Given the programme’s design, uptake is defined as the proportion of pregnant women who delivered in the reporting month and had received the RSV vaccine during pregnancy. This metric serves as a proxy for vaccine coverage by infant birth month, reflecting the extent of passive immunity conferred to newborns. This monthly report presents RSV vaccine uptake for women who delivered in the twenty-first month of the RSV vaccination programme in May 2026. The monthly uptake trend among pregnant women who have delivered since the programme’s launch is presented in Figure 1. Overall, the monthly RSV maternal vaccine uptake for May 2026 was 62.2%. RSV uptake increased in the first few months of the programme and has remained steady since October 2025. Figure 1. RSV vaccine uptake (%) trend among pregnant women by month of delivery, measured in May 2026 Note 1: the vertical lines represent a change in the percentage of GP (general practitioner) practices used to calculate RSV vaccine uptake. Up to December 2024, vaccine uptake was estimated based on data from a single supplier covering fewer than 40.5% of GP practices. From January 2025 onwards, vaccine uptake was based on data from more than 97.5% of GP practices and is more representative of national vaccination uptake. This month’s report includes data from both major GP IT suppliers, significantly expanding the data available in earlier reports (September to December 2024). It includes data from 98.7% of GPs in England, up from 40.4% of participating GPs previously in the first 4 months (September to December 2024) of the vaccination programme. This has been made possible by improvements in data quality and permits a more representative analysis of uptake and trends across England. To further explore variation in uptake, Table 1 presents uptake by commissioning region, while Table 2 provides the breakdown by ethnicity. As shown in Table 1, there are notable regional differences in uptake, with variation of up to 17.5 percentage points between NHS commissioning regions. Table 1. RSV vaccine uptake (%) in pregnant women, measured in May 2026, by NHS commissioning region Change to table view Commissioning region RSV uptake (%) North East and Yorkshire 62.8 North West 60.9 Midlands 57.7 East of England 65.5 London 54.8 South East 68.3 South West 72.3 Commissioning region RSV uptake (%) North East and Yorkshire 62.8 North West 60.9 Midlands 57.7 East of England 65.5 London 54.8 South East 68.3 South West 72.3 Variation in uptake by ethnicity was also observed, with a gap of 39.3 percentage points observed in the uptake between ethnic groups (Table 2). Table 2. RSV vaccine uptake (%) in pregnant women, measured in May 2026, by ethnicity Change to table view Ethnic group [note 2] RSV uptake (%) Asian or Asian British - any other Asian background 62.9 Asian or Asian British - Bangladeshi 55.8 Asian or Asian British - Chinese 78.5 Asian or Asian British - Indian 69.5 Asian or Asian British - Pakistani 46.6 Black or Black British - African 52.9 Black or Black British - any other Black background 44.7 Black or Black British - Caribbean 39.2 Mixed - any other mixed background 58.7 Mixed - White and Asian 64.6 Mixed - White and Black African 54.3 Mixed - White and Black Caribbean 42.6 White - British 68.2 White - Irish 59.9 White - any other White background 50.1 Any other ethnicity code 64.5 Ethnicity - unknown 57.5 Other ethnic group - any other ethnic group 48.0 Ethnic group [note 2] RSV uptake (%) Asian or Asian British - any other Asian background 62.9 Asian or Asian British - Bangladeshi 55.8 Asian or Asian British - Chinese 78.5 Asian or Asian British - Indian 69.5 Asian or Asian British - Pakistani 46.6 Black or Black British - African 52.9 Black or Black British - any other Black background 44.7 Black or Black British - Caribbean 39.2 Mixed - any other mixed background 58.7 Mixed - White and Asian 64.6 Mixed - White and Black African 54.3 Mixed - White and Black Caribbean 42.6 White - British 68.2 White - Irish 59.9 White - any other White background 50.1 Any other ethnicity code 64.5 Ethnicity - unknown 57.5 Other ethnic group - any other ethnic group 48.0 Note 2: the ‘Ethnicity - unknown’ group combines all records where ethnicity was not provided. This includes people whose ethnicity was not recorded, not stated, or who refused to give their ethnicity. The ‘Any other ethnicity code’ category includes individuals whose ethnicity has been recorded using non-standard or legacy codes (that is, codes not aligned with the 2001 or 2011 Census classifications). The map in figure 2 shows RSV uptake by ICB. Uptake varied across ICBs by 35.2 percentage points with the highest uptake reported in Norfolk and Waveney (76.3%) and the lowest uptake reported in Birmingham and Solihull (41.1%). Figure 2. RSV vaccine uptake (%) among pregnant women delivering in May 2026, by ICB Across the local authorities, uptake differed by 46.4 percentage points with the highest uptake reported in West Berkshire (82.3%) and the lowest uptake reported in Walsall (35.9%). The variation across the local authorities is presented in the map shown in Figure 3. Figure 3. RSV vaccine uptake (%) among pregnant women delivering in May 2026, by local authority Further detail, including uptake figures broken down by local authority and ICB, can be found in the May 2026 supplementary data tables. Since the RSV maternal vaccination programme has now been running for 21 months (up to the reporting month), an increasing number of pregnant women are receiving the vaccine during their eligible window. This growing awareness and notification from gestation week 20 onwards have contributed to a gradual increase in monthly vaccine uptake from 40.5% in September 2024 to the current figure reported for May 2026. As the programme continues and more women are informed earlier in their pregnancies, monthly vaccination uptake is expected to gradually increase. Data sources and methodology Further details on the data sources, methodology, data quality, and limitations are available in the quality and methodology information (QMI) report. The maternal RSV vaccine coverage estimates are calculated using monthly GP practice data automatically submitted to ImmForm by participating GP IT suppliers and validated and analysed by the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA). The report covers women who delivered during the reporting month (1 May 2026 to 31 May 2026), excluding miscarriages and stillbirths, with uptake measured as receipt of RSV vaccination from 28 weeks of pregnancy up to delivery. To ensure complete and accurate recording of vaccination and delivery information, data is extracted using a three-month reporting lag. The May 2026 estimates are based on data from the two major GP IT suppliers, representing 98.7% of participating GP practices nationally. The June 2026 maternal RSV vaccination uptake report is scheduled to be released on 5 November 2026. Background information The RSV vaccine has been offered to pregnant women in England since September 2024 to address the significant burden of RSV-related illness, hospitalisations and deaths, particularly among infants under 6 months of age and older adults, who are at increased risk of lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI) (see the Green Book on immunisation). In 2023, the Joint Committee on Vaccination and Immunisation (JCVI) issued a full statement recommending the implementation of a maternal RSV vaccination programme. This recommendation was based on robust evidence demonstrating the safety and effectiveness of RSV vaccines in protecting infants during their most vulnerable period. The vaccine is recommended as a year-round programme to be administered from 28 weeks of gestation onwards. This timing aligns with the optimal window for passive antibody transfer to the foetus, ensuring effective protection against severe RSV-related illness. From 1 September 2024 (the programme start date), all women who are at least 28 weeks pregnant are advised to receive the vaccine as soon as possible, with vaccination continuing to be recommended for all eligible women throughout pregnancy up until delivery. Additionally, the vaccine will be reoffered for every subsequent pregnancy to maintain consistent coverage and protection. This monthly report includes vaccine uptake data for women who delivered in May 2026. Programme delivery The programme is delivered through GP and maternity services, ensuring accessible vaccination opportunities for eligible pregnant women across England. In addition, the RSV vaccine is available through the community pharmacy delivery model at approximately 37 sites across two ICBs in the East of England. It is also available at up to 200 additional community pharmacy sites across the Midlands, North West, and London commissioning regions during the 2025 to 2026 expansion phase. Previous monthly reports are available at RSV maternal vaccination coverage in England. To view this licence, visit nationalarchives.gov.uk/doc/open-government-licence/version/3 or write to the Information Policy Team, The National Archives, Kew, London TW9 4DU, or email: psi@nationalarchives.gov.uk. Where we have identified any third party copyright information you will need to obtain permission from the copyright holders concerned. This publication is available at https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/respiratory-syncytial-virus-rsv-maternal-vaccination-coverage-in-england/respiratory-syncytial-virus-rsv-maternal-vaccination-coverage-in-england-may-2026-report Published 1 October 2026 This report presents monthly vaccine uptake data for the maternal respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) immunisation programme in England, focusing on the period up to May 2026. This report includes vaccine uptake estimates for pregnant women who delivered in the twenty-first month of the maternal vaccination programme in May 2026. Main points The main messages of this report are: 62.2% (26,174 out of 42,107) of women who reported giving birth during the survey month received an RSV vaccine uptake varied by NHS commissioning region, with the highest uptake reported in the South West region (72.3%) and the lowest in the London region (54.8%) uptake varied across integrated care boards (ICBs) with the highest uptake reported in the Norfolk and Waveney ICB (76.3%) and the lowest in Birmingham and Solihull ICB (41.1%) uptake varied across local authorities with the highest uptake reported in West Berkshire (82.3%) and the lowest in Walsall (35.9%) uptake varied by ethnic group, with the highest uptake reported among the Asian or Asian British - Chinese ethnic group (78.5%) and the lowest among the Black - Caribbean ethnic group (39.2%) Help us improve this resource This vaccine uptake report has been designated as an Official Statistics release. As part of this process, we are seeking feedback from users to ensure the publication meets your needs. We would be grateful if you could take a few minutes to complete a short survey and share your views. Please complete the survey Your input will play an important role in shaping the development of this publication. Thank you for your time and support. Analysis of maternal RSV vaccine uptake Maternal uptake of the RSV vaccine is assessed monthly to monitor the reach and impact of the national immunisation programme. Given the programme’s design, uptake is defined as the proportion of pregnant women who delivered in the reporting month and had received the RSV vaccine during pregnancy. This metric serves as a proxy for vaccine coverage by infant birth month, reflecting the extent of passive immunity conferred to newborns. This monthly report presents RSV vaccine uptake for women who delivered in the twenty-first month of the RSV vaccination programme in May 2026. The monthly uptake trend among pregnant women who have delivered since the programme’s launch is presented in Figure 1. Overall, the monthly RSV maternal vaccine uptake for May 2026 was 62.2%. RSV uptake increased in the first few months of the programme and has remained steady since October 2025. Figure 1. RSV vaccine uptake (%) trend among pregnant women by month of delivery, measured in May 2026 Note 1: the vertical lines represent a change in the percentage of GP (general practitioner) practices used to calculate RSV vaccine uptake. Up to December 2024, vaccine uptake was estimated based on data from a single supplier covering fewer than 40.5% of GP practices. From January 2025 onwards, vaccine uptake was based on data from more than 97.5% of GP practices and is more representative of national vaccination uptake. This month’s report includes data from both major GP IT suppliers, significantly expanding the data available in earlier reports (September to December 2024). It includes data from 98.7% of GPs in England, up from 40.4% of participating GPs previously in the first 4 months (September to December 2024) of the vaccination programme. This has been made possible by improvements in data quality and permits a more representative analysis of uptake and trends across England. To further explore variation in uptake, Table 1 presents uptake by commissioning region, while Table 2 provides the breakdown by ethnicity. As shown in Table 1, there are notable regional differences in uptake, with variation of up to 17.5 percentage points between NHS commissioning regions. Table 1. RSV vaccine uptake (%) in pregnant women, measured in May 2026, by NHS commissioning region Change to table view Commissioning region RSV uptake (%) North East and Yorkshire 62.8 North West 60.9 Midlands 57.7 East of England 65.5 London 54.8 South East 68.3 South West 72.3 Commissioning region RSV uptake (%) North East and Yorkshire 62.8 North West 60.9 Midlands 57.7 East of England 65.5 London 54.8 South East 68.3 South West 72.3 Variation in uptake by ethnicity was also observed, with a gap of 39.3 percentage points observed in the uptake between ethnic groups (Table 2). Table 2. RSV vaccine uptake (%) in pregnant women, measured in May 2026, by ethnicity Change to table view Ethnic group [note 2] RSV uptake (%) Asian or Asian British - any other Asian background 62.9 Asian or Asian British - Bangladeshi 55.8 Asian or Asian British - Chinese 78.5 Asian or Asian British - Indian 69.5 Asian or Asian British - Pakistani 46.6 Black or Black British - African 52.9 Black or Black British - any other Black background 44.7 Black or Black British - Caribbean 39.2 Mixed - any other mixed background 58.7 Mixed - White and Asian 64.6 Mixed - White and Black African 54.3 Mixed - White and Black Caribbean 42.6 White - British 68.2 White - Irish 59.9 White - any other White background 50.1 Any other ethnicity code 64.5 Ethnicity - unknown 57.5 Other ethnic group - any other ethnic group 48.0 Ethnic group [note 2] RSV uptake (%) Asian or Asian British - any other Asian background 62.9 Asian or Asian British - Bangladeshi 55.8 Asian or Asian British - Chinese 78.5 Asian or Asian British - Indian 69.5 Asian or Asian British - Pakistani 46.6 Black or Black British - African 52.9 Black or Black British - any other Black background 44.7 Black or Black British - Caribbean 39.2 Mixed - any other mixed background 58.7 Mixed - White and Asian 64.6 Mixed - White and Black African 54.3 Mixed - White and Black Caribbean 42.6 White - British 68.2 White - Irish 59.9 White - any other White background 50.1 Any other ethnicity code 64.5 Ethnicity - unknown 57.5 Other ethnic group - any other ethnic group 48.0 Note 2: the ‘Ethnicity - unknown’ group combines all records where ethnicity was not provided. This includes people whose ethnicity was not recorded, not stated, or who refused to give their ethnicity. The ‘Any other ethnicity code’ category includes individuals whose ethnicity has been recorded using non-standard or legacy codes (that is, codes not aligned with the 2001 or 2011 Census classifications). The map in figure 2 shows RSV uptake by ICB. Uptake varied across ICBs by 35.2 percentage points with the highest uptake reported in Norfolk and Waveney (76.3%) and the lowest uptake reported in Birmingham and Solihull (41.1%). Figure 2. RSV vaccine uptake (%) among pregnant women delivering in May 2026, by ICB Across the local authorities, uptake differed by 46.4 percentage points with the highest uptake reported in West Berkshire (82.3%) and the lowest uptake reported in Walsall (35.9%). The variation across the local authorities is presented in the map shown in Figure 3. Figure 3. RSV vaccine uptake (%) among pregnant women delivering in May 2026, by local authority Further detail, including uptake figures broken down by local authority and ICB, can be found in the May 2026 supplementary data tables. Since the RSV maternal vaccination programme has now been running for 21 months (up to the reporting month), an increasing number of pregnant women are receiving the vaccine during their eligible window. This growing awareness and notification from gestation week 20 onwards have contributed to a gradual increase in monthly vaccine uptake from 40.5% in September 2024 to the current figure reported for May 2026. As the programme continues and more women are informed earlier in their pregnancies, monthly vaccination uptake is expected to gradually increase. Data sources and methodology Further details on the data sources, methodology, data quality, and limitations are available in the quality and methodology information (QMI) report. The maternal RSV vaccine coverage estimates are calculated using monthly GP practice data automatically submitted to ImmForm by participating GP IT suppliers and validated and analysed by the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA). The report covers women who delivered during the reporting month (1 May 2026 to 31 May 2026), excluding miscarriages and stillbirths, with uptake measured as receipt of RSV vaccination from 28 weeks of pregnancy up to delivery. To ensure complete and accurate recording of vaccination and delivery information, data is extracted using a three-month reporting lag. The May 2026 estimates are based on data from the two major GP IT suppliers, representing 98.7% of participating GP practices nationally. The June 2026 maternal RSV vaccination uptake report is scheduled to be released on 5 November 2026. Background information The RSV vaccine has been offered to pregnant women in England since September 2024 to address the significant burden of RSV-related illness, hospitalisations and deaths, particularly among infants under 6 months of age and older adults, who are at increased risk of lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI) (see the Green Book on immunisation). In 2023, the Joint Committee on Vaccination and Immunisation (JCVI) issued a full statement recommending the implementation of a maternal RSV vaccination programme. This recommendation was based on robust evidence demonstrating the safety and effectiveness of RSV vaccines in protecting infants during their most vulnerable period. The vaccine is recommended as a year-round programme to be administered from 28 weeks of gestation onwards. This timing aligns with the optimal window for passive antibody transfer to the foetus, ensuring effective protection against severe RSV-related illness. From 1 September 2024 (the programme start date), all women who are at least 28 weeks pregnant are advised to receive the vaccine as soon as possible, with vaccination continuing to be recommended for all eligible women throughout pregnancy up until delivery. Additionally, the vaccine will be reoffered for every subsequent pregnancy to maintain consistent coverage and protection. This monthly report includes vaccine uptake data for women who delivered in May 2026. Programme delivery The programme is delivered through GP and maternity services, ensuring accessible vaccination opportunities for eligible pregnant women across England. In addition, the RSV vaccine is available through the community pharmacy delivery model at approximately 37 sites across two ICBs in the East of England. It is also available at up to 200 additional community pharmacy sites across the Midlands, North West, and London commissioning regions during the 2025 to 2026 expansion phase. Previous monthly reports are available at RSV maternal vaccination coverage in England. analysis.time: The report was published on 1 October 2026. The data refers to the period up to May 2026, with the vaccine uptake measured for women who delivered in May 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: The report focuses on England, specifically on NHS commissioning regions and integrated care boards (ICBs) within the country. It includes data on pregnant women across different ethnic groups.
analysis.event: The report details the maternal RSV vaccination coverage in England as of May 2026, including uptake rates by NHS commissioning region, ICB, and ethnic group. It is an official statistics release by the UK Health Security Agency.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The RSV vaccine uptake in May 2026 was 62.2% among women who delivered during that month. Uptake varied significantly by region, with the highest at 72.3% in the South West and lowest at 54.8% in London. It also varied by ICB, with the highest at 76.3% in Norfolk and Waveney and lowest at 41.1% in Birmingham and Solihull. Ethnic group differences were also noted, with the highest uptake among the Asian or Asian British - Chinese group (78.5%) and lowest among the Black - Caribbean group (39.2%).
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The report is an official statistics release and includes data from both major GP IT suppliers, covering 98.7% of GPs in England. It notes improvements in data quality and a more representative analysis of uptake since January 2025. The data is based on a three-month reporting lag to ensure completeness and accuracy.

analysis.brief_en: The UK Health Security Agency released an official statistics report on 1 October 2026 detailing the maternal RSV vaccination coverage in England as of May 2026. The report highlights that 62.2% of pregnant women who delivered in May 2026 received the RSV vaccine, with regional variations observed. The highest uptake was recorded in the South West region at 72.3%, while London had the lowest at 54.8%. Integrated care boards (ICBs) also showed significant differences, with Norfolk and Waveney reporting 76.3% uptake and Birmingham and Solihull at 41.1%. Ethnic group disparities were noted, with the Asian or Asian British - Chinese group having the highest uptake at 78.5% and the Black - Caribbean group the lowest at 39.2%. The data, collected from 98.7% of GPs in England, reflects improvements in data quality since January 2025, allowing for a more representative analysis of vaccine coverage. The report serves as a monitoring tool for the national immunisation programme targeting RSV-related illnesses in infants and older adults.

news.source_body_en: The UK Health Security Agency released an official statistics report on 1 October 2026 detailing the maternal RSV vaccination coverage in England as of May 2026. The report highlights that 62.2% of pregnant women who delivered in May 2026 received the RSV vaccine, with regional variations observed. The highest uptake was recorded in the South West region at 72.3%, while London had the lowest at 54.8%. Integrated care boards (ICBs) also showed significant differences, with Norfolk and Waveney reporting 76.3% uptake and Birmingham and Solihull at 41.1%. Ethnic group disparities were noted, with the Asian or Asian British - Chinese group having the highest uptake at 78.5% and the Black - Caribbean group the lowest at 39.2%. The data, collected from 98.7% of GPs in England, reflects improvements in data quality since January 2025, allowing for a more representative analysis of vaccine coverage. news.content_zh: 英国卫生安全局于2026年10月1日发布了一份官方统计数据报告,详细说明了截至2026年5月英格兰的母体呼吸道合胞病毒 疫苗接种 覆盖率。报告指出,2026年5月分娩的孕妇中有62.2%接受了呼吸道合胞病毒 疫苗 接种,存在地区差异。最高接种率出现在西南地区,为72.3%,而伦敦的接种率最低,为54.8%。综合照护委员会(ICBs)之间也存在显著差异,诺福克和韦内地区报告接种率为76.3%,而伯明翰和索利胡尔地区仅为41.1%。在种族群体方面,亚洲或亚洲英国-中国群体的接种率最高,为78.5%,而黑人-加勒比群体的接种率最低,为39.2%。数据来自英格兰98.7%的全科医生(GPs),反映了自2025年1月起数据质量的提升,使得对疫苗接种率的分析更具代表性。该报告作为针对婴儿和老年人呼吸道合胞病毒相关疾病的国家免疫计划的监测工具。

Director of Health Department Resources Department Homepage About the Health Department About Us Frequently Asked Questions Career Opportunities Contact Us Department Divisions Emergency Preparedness & Response Environmental Health Laboratory Services School Health Health Department Services Health Department Programs Disease Carrying Insects - Fight the Bite Homeless Healthcare Program Public Health Youth Ambassadors Stable Families, Thriving Futures Strengthening Antimicrobial Stewardship Clinic Locations Diseases & Conditions Health Alerts & Advisories News & Events Permits & Health Codes 2026-2027 Respiratory Illness Season: How to Protect Against Flu, COVID-19 and RSV October 5, 2026 Now that fall has arrived, respiratory season is here and the number of people getting sick with a respiratory illness is expected to increase. Although germs will be circulating over the next few months, there are many ways to stay healthy and protect yourself from flu, COVID-19, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). Remember, vaccination is your first line of defense against respiratory diseases. Vaccine Recommendations for 2026-2027 Respiratory Illness Season: Children (6 months–18 years): Annual flu shot for all; annual COVID-19 for ages 6–23 months and for ages 2–18 in certain risk groups (optional otherwise); RSV vaccine for infants under 8 months if the mother was not vaccinated in pregnancy, and for ages 8–19 months in certain risk groups. Healthy adults (19–64 years): Annual flu and COVID-19 vaccines for all; one-time RSV vaccine for adults 50–74 at increased risk, in consultation with a healthcare provider. Pregnant women: Annual flu (no nasal spray) and updated COVID-19 vaccines; RSV vaccine at 32–36 weeks’ gestation (Sept 1–March 1) each pregnancy to protect newborns. Older adults (65+ years): Annual high-dose flu vaccine and annual COVID-19 vaccine plus a booster after 6 months; one-time RSV vaccine for all adults 75 and older. Immunocompromised (6 months+): Annual flu (no nasal spray) and COVID-19 vaccines; RSV vaccine considered on a case‐by‐case basis with a healthcare provider. When to get it: The ideal time is by the end of October, but you can still get vaccinated later in the season. Flu viruses usually start increasing in early October, peak in January or February, and can circulate through late May. What’s in the vaccine: The current flu shot protects against three flu virus strains, including the influenza A(H3N2) subclade K virus that spread widely during the 2025–2026 season. COVID-19 COVID-19 vaccines are available for everyone 6 months and older. Who especially needs it: Older adults, infants, and people who are pregnant are strongly encouraged to be vaccinated because they are at higher risk of severe illness. Why an updated dose matters: Protection from COVID-19 vaccines decreases over time, so getting an updated dose (if you are eligible) helps restore and maintain protection. Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) Adults: All adults 75 years and older should receive a single dose of an RSV vaccine. Adults aged 50–74 with certain health conditions should talk with their healthcare provider to decide if the RSV vaccine is appropriate, as some conditions increase the risk of severe RSV. Babies and Pregnancy: All babies should be protected from severe RSV using one of two options: A maternal RSV vaccine given during pregnancy, or An RSV monoclonal antibody given directly to the baby. These options significantly reduce the risk of hospitalization for infants during their first RSV season. Pregnant people and parents of newborns should talk with their healthcare providers about the best RSV protection for their baby. Talk with your health care provider for details. Wash hands often with soap and water for 20 seconds, especially after coughing or sneezing. Cover coughs and sneezes with a tissue or your elbow. Stay home if you are sick with respiratory illness to prevent spreading it to others. Return to normal activity when your symptoms have improved, and you are fever free for 24 hours. Keep a distance from others when possible. Improve air quality by bringing in fresh air from outside (opening doors or windows or using exhaust fans), purifying air indoors, or gathering outdoors. Help spread the message about respiratory illness. Share Respiratory Illness Resources with your friends, family, school, or health clinic. news.content_title: RSV-B Bronchiolitis Linked to More Severe Wheezing, Night Cough Than RSV-A at School Age
news.content: Clinical Hub News & Perspective Tools & Reference CME/CE More NEW! Ask complex medical questions and find the latest clinical guidance for drugs & conditions with Medscape AI× EN RegisterLog In AI Mode Medscape Medical NewsMedBrief Medbrief RSV-B Bronchiolitis Linked to More Severe Wheezing, Night Cough Than RSV-A at School Age October 01, 2026 0 Add to Email Alerts TOPLINE Among children and adolescents hospitalized for severe bronchiolitis in the first 2 years of life, those whose illness was caused by respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) subgroup B were more likely than those with RSV subgroup A to report wheezing that restricted speech and nighttime dry cough at school age, whereas current asthma prevalence and lung function did not differ significantly. METHODOLOGY This prospective, cross-sectional study conducted from September 2023 to June 2025 in Madrid, Spain, included 185 children and adolescents (age, 5-18 years; 53.5% boys) who had been hospitalized for severe bronchiolitis caused by RSV subgroup A or B. They were assessed at a follow-up visit, and their medium-term respiratory outcomes were compared by RSV subgroup (A vs B). All participants had been hospitalized during the first 2 years of life, between 2004 and 2017, for bronchiolitis caused by a single RSV infection: 129 with subgroup A and 56 with subgroup B. Current asthma was defined as wheezing or whistling sounds from the chest during the previous 12 months, reported by families on a Spanish-validated asthma symptom questionnaire. The same questionnaire also included questions on severe wheezing that restricted speech and nighttime dry cough unrelated to infections. Participants underwent lung function testing, an exhaled nitric oxide test, and skin-prick tests for sensitization to common airborne allergens. TAKEAWAY Severe wheezing that restricted speech was more common among children previously hospitalized for bronchiolitis caused by RSV-B than among those hospitalized for bronchiolitis caused by RSV-A (odds ratio [OR], 2.62; 95% CI, 1.3-5.4). Nighttime dry cough unrelated to infections was also more frequent among the children hospitalized for bronchiolitis caused by RSV-B than RSV-A (16.9% vs 7.7%; P = .044). In adjusted analyses, prior bronchiolitis caused by RSV-B was independently associated with nighttime dry cough (OR, 3.98; P = .018), alongside allergic rhinitis, maternal asthma, and maternal smoking during pregnancy. Current asthma rates, lung function, exhaled nitric oxide levels, and allergic sensitization were not significantly different across the two groups. IN PRACTICE "[S]ince a history of HRSV-B [human RSV subgroup B] bronchiolitis appears to be associated with a poorer prognosis, closer monitoring of this patient group—with better medical management of respiratory symptoms during the first years of life—could lead to reduced medium-term morbidity," the authors wrote. SOURCE The study was led by María Arroyas Sánchez, Severo Ochoa University Hospital, Madrid, Spain. It was published online on September 20, 2026, in Pediatric Pulmonology. LIMITATIONS The study's sample size fell short of the target, and it included far fewer children in the RSV-B group than in the RSV-A group. Symptoms were assessed at a single visit and relied on recall, and many eligible patients did not enroll, mostly for logistical reasons; therefore, recall and selection bias may have affected the results. DISCLOSURES The study was funded by Merck, Sharp & Dohme, Horizon Europe, and Instituto de Salud Carlos III. The authors reported having no conflicts of interest. In adjusted analyses, prior bronchiolitis caused by RSV-B was independently associated with nighttime dry cough (OR, 3.98; P = .018), alongside allergic rhinitis, maternal asthma, and maternal smoking during pregnancy. Current asthma rates, lung function, exhaled nitric oxide levels, and allergic sensitization were not significantly different across the two groups. IN PRACTICE "[S]ince a history of HRSV-B [human RSV subgroup B] bronchiolitis appears to be associated with a poorer prognosis, closer monitoring of this patient group—with better medical management of respiratory symptoms during the first years of life—could lead to reduced medium-term morbidity," the authors wrote. SOURCE The study was led by María Arroyas Sánchez, Severo Ochoa University Hospital, Madrid, Spain. It was published online on September 20, 2026, in Pediatric Pulmonology. LIMITATIONS The study's sample size fell short of the target, and it included far fewer children in the RSV-B group than in the RSV-A group. Symptoms were assessed at a single visit and relied on recall, and many eligible patients did not enroll, mostly for logistical reasons; therefore, recall and selection bias may have affected the results. DISCLOSURES The study was funded by Merck, Sharp & Dohme, Horizon Europe, and Instituto de Salud Carlos III. The authors reported having no conflicts of interest. news.content_zh: 一项于2026年9月20日发表在《Pediatric Pulmonology》上的研究发现,与由RSV-A引起的毛细支气管炎住院的儿童相比,由RSV-B引起的严重毛细支气管炎住院的儿童在学龄期更可能报告限制言语的严重喘息和夜间干咳。该研究于2023年9月至2025年6月在西班牙马德里进行,纳入了185名5-18岁儿童,这些儿童在出生后的前两年内因单次RSV感染住院治疗了毛细支气管炎。研究使用了经过西班牙验证的哮喘症状问卷来评估呼吸系统结局。尽管RSV-B组的严重喘息和夜间干咳更为常见,但当前哮喘患病率、肺功能、呼出一氧化氮水平和过敏原致敏情况在两组之间并无显著差异。该研究存在局限性,包括RSV-B样本量较小以及基于回忆的症状报告,这可能引入偏倚。作者建议,对有RSV-B 毛细支气管炎病史的儿童进行更密切的监测,有助于更好地管理呼吸症状并减少中长期发病率。
